title: Projected Share of Operating Costs for Thomson-East Coast MRT Line to be Covered by Fare Revenues Versus Government Subsidies
what_it_is: Projected Share of Operating Costs for Thomson-East Coast MRT Line to be Covered by Fare Revenues Versus Government Subsidies

sections.label: MRT network expansion spending
sections.summary: The Government will spend about $25 billion over the next five years to expand the MRT network.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: For instance, over the next five years, the Government will be spending about $25 billion to expand our Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) network.

sections.label: Rail operating assets upgrade spending
sections.summary: The Government will spend around $4.5 billion over five years to build up, replace and upgrade rail operating assets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Second, the Government will be spending around $4.5 billion over the next five years to build up, replace and upgrade rail operating assets on the rail network, including trains, signaling systems and power supply systems.

sections.label: SMRT and SBST losses
sections.summary: SMRT Trains reported an $86 million loss and SBST's Downtown Line a loss of more than $47 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: In the financial year ended 31 March 2018, SMRT Trains reported a loss of $86 million, against an operating cost of $838 million and commuters' fare income of $608 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: In another example, SBST's Downtown Line also incurred a loss of more than $47 million for the financial year ended 31 December 2017, against an operating cost of $132 million and commuters' fare income of $69 million.

sections.label: TEL revenue risk arrangement
sections.summary: The Government bears revenue risk for TEL's first nine-year concession, collecting fares and paying SMRT a service fee.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: But the fixed overhead cost is sunk and the operator has to shoulder that.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: And that is why the Government decided to bear the revenue risk by subjecting TEL to an arrangement similar to public buses, for its first concession period of nine years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Under this model, the Government collects fare revenue and pays the operator, SMRT, a service fee for O&M.

sections.label: MKBF data encouraging
sections.summary: The MKBF data released last week are extremely encouraging.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: The MKBF data that were released last week are extremely encouraging.

sections.label: Thomson Line subsidy implication
sections.summary: At Year 9, fares will be less than half of Thomson Line's operating costs, implying significant Government subsidy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Back to this Thomson Line, for the first concession period of nine years, at Year 9, we are talking about fares – assuming today's fares and adjusted through the fare formula – will be less than 50%, less than half of the operating costs of Thomson Line at Year 9.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: This implies a very significant subsidy on the part of the Government.

sections.label: PTC formula and operating cost
sections.summary: The PTC formula has not accounted for the substantial increase in operating cost needed to fix the reliability problem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: The PTC formula, as noted by the Member, has not taken into account the substantial increase in operating cost in order to fix the reliability problem.

sections.label: Reliability as engineering problem
sections.summary: Reliability is an engineering problem that can be fixed but requires money, resources and time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: What we have learnt in the last three years is that reliability is an engineering problem; it can be fixed but you need money, you need resources and you need time.
